paragraphs.text: A simple popup that can quickly show when Deepseek has finished thinking or is requesting permission
during split-screen.
# dsh-thinking-notifier
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that shows a small **always-on-top desktop popup** in the bottom-rig
ht corner of your screen. It mirrors the AI's thinking status in real time and alerts you when the A
I **requests permission**, **waits for a choice from you**, or **finishes thinking** — even when you
are working in other apps, browsers, or virtual desktops.
> 中文说明见 README.zh.md
## Features
| State | Popup | Sound |
| AI is thinking | DeepSeek-blue pulsing dot + `AI 正在思考…` + elapsed time. Auto-collapses to a 25 px

slim right-edge tab after 5 s; hover or click the tab to expand it again | none |
| AI waits for you
r choice | Violet pulsing dot + `AI 正在等待你的选择` + the question heading, the first question's option la
bels (`选项：A / B`, `（可多选）` for multi-select, `（共 N 问）` when several questions arrive at once) and how

long it has been waiting. Stays expanded until you answer | system Question |
| AI requests permiss
ion | Amber pulsing dot + `AI 请求权限` + session/tool name. Stays expanded until you decide | system Ex

clamation |
| AI finished thinking | Green dot + `AI 已完成思考`, auto-hides after 12 s | system Asterisk

|
| Idle | Hidden | none |

- DeepSeek-style dark card (`#1E2235` / `#4D6BFE`).
- Always-on-top frameless window, bottom-right,

visible over any application.
- Auto-collapses into a 25 px slim right-edge tab after 5 s while the

AI is thinking, so it stays visible without blocking desktop controls.
- Hover or click the edge tab
to expand it manually; new turns, questions, permission requests, and completions expand it automat

ically.
- Click the **X** button to dismiss the current popup; the next new turn, question, permissi

on request, or completion will show it again.
- Questions are shown with their options, which is eno
ugh to know what is being decided; the answer itself is still given in the DSH Web UI (the popup is

read-only by design).
- Multiple sessions are summarized automatically.
- The popup process stays al

ive while DSH runs; it exits ~15 s after the status endpoint becomes unreachable.
- No browser exten
sion required; the popup is a native desktop window.

`pendingKind` is `approval` or `question`. `timeText` is the th
inking timer while `running` and the waiting time while `question`; `detailText` carries the first q
`running` and the waiting time while `question`; `detailText` carries the first question's options.

## Configuration
| Environment variable | Default | Description |
| `DSH_THINKING_NOTIFIER_PORT` | `7389` | Local status server port. If busy, the next 10 ports are t

ried. |
| `DSH_THINKING_NOTIFIER_NO_POPUP` | unset | Set to `1` to run the status server without lau
nching the desktop popup (headless, tests). |
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness Web UI (`dsh web`)
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`
- Windows: Windows 10/11 with

PowerShell 5.1+ (built in)
- macOS/Linux: Python 3 with `tkinter`
## Verification status
Being explicit about what has actually been tested, so nobody is surprised:
| Area | Status |
| Thinking / done states, popup geometry, sounds, single instance | verified on Windows 10/11 (Power

Shell 5.1 + WPF) |
| Question state (`ask_user_question`) | verified end to end in a live DSH sessio
n (a real question drove the popup into the waiting state, and it cleared when the answer arrived),

against the real `ctx.userQuestions` service in a cordis context, and by the smoke test |
| Permissi
on alert (amber) | **verified only with the mock status service.** On a Windows DSH install without
a confining sandbox, an out-of-workspace write is not intercepted, so no approval is raised by the r
untime; the request only appears when a tool call explicitly asks for a `sandbox_permissions` escala

tion or a pre-execute hook returns `ask` |
| `desktop-popup.py` (macOS/Linux) | **never run on real

hardware** — syntax-checked only |
| Popup process stacking after repeated `dsh web` restarts | the
launcher kills stale popups for its own port before starting a new one; verified for a single restar
kills stale popups for its own port before starting a new one; verified for a single restart cycle |
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use a spare port for popup experiments: the real popup on `7389` is left alone, because the plugin o
nly cleans up popup processes belonging to its own port.

## Troubleshooting
Debug logs are written to:

- `~/.dsh/tn-plugin.log` — host plugin lifecycle, popup launcher, question watcher.
- `~/.dsh/tn-lau

ncher.log` — PID of the popup process created by the launcher.
- `~/.dsh/tn-popup-debug.log` — popup
script lifecycle and polling errors.

If the popup does not appear after restarting `dsh web`, check those logs first.
Note that `popup la
uncher exit: code=0` in `tn-plugin.log` is expected: the plugin spawns a one-shot launcher which sta
rts the real popup process and then exits.
